variants.name: 灰石山墙老警署
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one complete architectural design board for Wrong Date Testimony, a first-person mystery game set in a fictional small town in January 1931. Original fictional architecture, no national police branding.
Create a polished wide landscape board with FOUR well-separated visual panels in a 2x2 composition: upper left street-level three-quarter exterior of the ENTIRE building; upper right eye-level interior of its public records room; lower left roof-removed isometric GROUND-floor spatial model; lower right separate roof-removed isometric UPPER-floor spatial model. Small inset along bottom for period desk objects. Every view depicts the SAME building with the same coherent shell, doors and two actual floor levels. Upper floor must be a real enclosed usable floor with corresponding exterior windows; NO fake decorative extra levels, basement, towers, or attic floor. Isometrics are spatial concept illustrations, NOT technical blueprints.
All proposals fit a 23m wide by 39m deep lot. SOUTH street front, central south entrance, north service courtyard and rear exit. Human-scale doors, accessible circulating hall, clear stairs between the two floors. Give priority to practical furnishings and full rooms, no maze. Include public reception, records reading room, interview room, stored evidence, one small former holding room, duty office, staff rest space and toilets. Holding room is a small secondary room, not a large prison.
Narrative emphasis is paper-based investigation: warm shaded reading lamps, bound registers, file boxes, numbered-looking drawer pulls without readable numbers, blank folded document copies, a wood document cradle, separate photo mounts with indistinct gray surfaces. NO explicit new clue, no murder weapon, no answers or readable evidence text. No prisoner, blood, corpse, portrait suspects, detective strings, accusation board or torture equipment. No people at all. NO modern monitors, fluorescent tubes, CCTV, walkie-talkies, plastic chairs, fluorescent emergency-exit signs, police cars, barbed wire, modern badges or weapons.
Style: premium stylized 3D environmental concept art, crisp simplified geometry and broad low-saturation material areas, subtle wood/stone/metal texture, the visual family of the project's cream-stone timber clocktower, deep-green walnut watch shop, timber milk shop and iron-and-glass station. Soft neutral gray overcast January dusk and wet paving outside, warm amber task lighting inside, readable shadows rather than pitch black or blue-cyan grading. Calm lived-in working building, cared for but worn. No photoreal photographic collage and no cartoon candy palette.
Text: Only the proposal letter and its short English name in a restrained top margin. No other labels, letters, room names, dates, logos or watermark. Reserve room names and exact dimensions for a separately authored plan.
Proposal A title text: "A · STONE GABLES".
Architecture: dignified OLD GRAY STONE station; long 23x12m two-storey street range, a low 7.6x7m wing projecting behind the EAST end, forming an L. Pale warm-gray rough-cut stone, dark slate pitched roof with two end gables and a restrained central entrance gable; there are TWO floors only beneath the pitched roof, no attic windows. Dark moss-green paneled central door, small stone hood and a pair of warm iron wall lamps. Fine regular sash windows, quiet civic scale, no grand courthouse columns.
Ground: left/west front is a welcoming public reading room with two large oak tables and wall records shelves; center reception axis gives direct access to it without walking behind the staff counter; right/east front reception/duty work; rear center corridor, west interview room, east stairs. Small low rear east wing holds old holding room and stored evidence.
Upper: chief/duty offices, archive storage and staff rest around a short hall; NO public balcony. Records interior shows stone deep window reveals, warm oak paneling, faded olive cabinets, cream upper walls, desk lamp on blank register, street visible through real windows. Layout atmosphere: reassuring order at entrance, quieter tension only in the rear.

Proposal B title text: "B · BRICK PATROL YARD".
Architecture: utilitarian RED-BRICK working station, long 23x12m TWO-storey main block with restrained asymmetry, very low gray slate hipped roof, stone lintels and gray-green wood sash frames; 7.6x7m SINGLE-storey east rear service/cell wing. No sawtooth industrial factory, no extra tower or floor. Thin black iron porch over center south entrance, solid simple wood gate north. A modest bicycle lean-to, coat/rain cape hooks seen through service door, coal and timber store in rear yard, NO vehicles.
Ground circulation: entrance center, reception and document tables front CENTER/RIGHT, wide north-south west corridor leading to courtyard; WEST FRONT interview room, RIGHT FRONT public records room separated by a translucent glass-and-timber partition from duty desks; rear duty work, upper stair along west side; old holding/evidence rooms in rear east wing with tiny high windows.
Upper has a long east-west duty hall, patrol paperwork desks, archive shelves and small rest/mess area. Records-room interior has red brick lower wall, muted sage-gray painted timber wainscot, darker pine desks, amber brass task lamps and buff files; visible administrative bustle conveyed by objects alone. Strong horizontal brick mass, quiet workaday civic realism, distinct from romantic stone gables.

Proposal C title text: "C · IVORY CIVIC".
Architecture: restrained EARLY INTERWAR GEOMETRIC public station, two actual floors in a 23x12m box, ivory plaster and pale stone base, dark petrol-blue door frames, thin aged brass accents. Flat roofs with shallow stepped parapets; central entrance bay is a modest risalit SAME roof height, no tall tower and no extra floor. Symmetrical vertical grouped windows on both occupied floors, NOT enormous modern glass curtain wall. Single-storey 7.6x7m low flat-roof east rear wing. Monolithic clean calm horizontal silhouette with a subtle vertical rhythm.
Ground: CENTRAL low desk reception and open reading hall, public case records accessible on two reading tables on WEST side; east interview room, north administrative hall behind timber/glass partitions, stair EAST rear; evidence/former holding low wing north-east.
Upper: central hallway, west municipal archive/reference work area, east detective/duty office and staff rest. No open mezzanine, two real enclosed floors. Records interior has ivory walls, petrol-blue joinery, dark walnut flat-front cabinets, warm opal glass pendant lamps and brass desk lamps, gray terrazzo-like floor, warm wooden reading tables. Strong precise geometry and generous clear sightlines, no overt modernism or late-streamlined luxury style.

Proposal D title text: "D · COURTYARD LOGGIA".
Architecture: SMALL U-SHAPED COURTYARD station contained in the same 23x39m lot. Front south block 23x12m TWO occupied storeys, cream-gray lime-plastered masonry, muted warm-gray stone base, DARK slate shallow hipped roof. Two SINGLE-storey rear wings each 5.5m wide extend 12m NORTH beyond the front block, leaving a 12m-wide open-air inner court. Ground covered timber colonnade runs inside U around an open wet stone court with a restrained bare tree and bench; no third closing building that blocks north exit. Roofs have no attic windows. SOUTH central entrance goes through reception and out into the open court; north exit gate beyond court. This uses a deeper plot than the other proposals but no wider one.
Ground: public reading room left/west front accessible immediately from reception; east front interview room and enclosed stairs; WEST court wing large bound-file archive and quiet reading annex; EAST court wing duty room, stored evidence and one tiny old holding room at north end. All wings actually have rooms with real corresponding windows.
Upper exists ONLY above FRONT block, with offices, archive cataloguing and staff rest on short corridor; do not depict a complete upper U or invent upper wing rooms. Main interior view: records reading room with a large real courtyard window, cream walls, pale oak shelves, dark iron lamps, rain visible beyond colonnade. Mood: spacious quiet intervals, rain and warm paper-lit shelter, an elegant intimate civic compound, NOT palace or medieval cloister.

Proposal E title text: "E · HOUSE AND ARCHIVE".
Architecture: an OLD TWO-STOREY HOUSE adapted into a small police archive station, 18m wide x12m deep compact main block centered on south entry within the 23m plot; small 6x7m SINGLE-storey east rear attachment. Warm muted buff-gray plaster, aged BURGUNDY wood door and shutters, weathered dark timber accents, asymmetric intersecting pitched slate roofs but ONLY two floors and no dormers/attic. Modest deep central entrance porch, a side projecting first-floor room supported by existing masonry, no fancy mansion columns or fake upper balconies. North garden/service yard enclosed by ordinary low walls with open passage to rear gate. Distinct domestic scale and irregular window grouping, no symmetric institutional front.
Ground: former front parlor WEST transformed into cozy PUBLIC case-file reading room with domestic fireplace and oval wooden table; former front dining room EAST now reception/duty desks; main stair center rear, west rear interview room, east rear evidence and service room, tiny old holding room in rear attachment. Clear central passage through to rear courtyard independent of reading table.
Upper: intimate large archive/reference room across west and central main block, cataloguing tables and shelving; east duty/chief office and rest room. Record-view interior shows repurposed house trim, muted burgundy paneling, old walnut cupboards, paper drawers, amber lamp, curtains pulled clear of real windows. Cozy yet uneasy, wood creaks and old ordinary domestic rooms performing institutional work. Not haunted ruin, horror dungeon or aristocratic luxury.
